description: Alternative to the PCA-based (ZEUS) vibrato edits in run1-3: uses the same repo's TEXT-based editing mode (ZETA, main_run.py) instead. Fully deterministic given fixed inputs -- no PCA/power-iteration, no eigenvector sign ambiguity, no uncalibrated eigenvalue, no hand-picked PC index. Source and target prompts kept nearly identical except the inserted vibrato phrase, following the paper's own convention (Fig. 3: 'bold marks changed text') so the model localizes the edit to that one attribute rather than regenerating everything.
input_audio: same 16-second clip as run2/run3 (first 16s of full MDDBGospel.mp3)

model.source_prompt: A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing, and drums and guitar playing.
model.target_prompt: A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing with a strong vocal vibrato, and drums and guitar playing.
model.note: only the inserted phrase 'with a strong vocal vibrato' differs between source and target

command: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python main_run.py --init_aud MDDBGospel_16sec.wav --model_id cvssp/audioldm2-music --source_prompt "A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing, and drums and guitar playing." --target_prompt "A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing with a strong vocal vibrato, and drums and guitar playing." --tstart 100 --results_path results_zeta_vibrato

key_parameters.note_on_determinism: no seed needed for reproducibility of the EDIT DIRECTION itself (unlike ZEUS/PCA) since there's no random power-iteration involved -- same source/target prompt pair always specifies the same semantic direction. A seed would only matter for exact bit-reproducibility of the model's internal sampling, not for which concept gets edited.

runtime.wallclock_sec: ~53s total (200-step inversion + 100-step generation, since tstart=100 skips the first 100 of 200 generation steps)

repo_quirk_found.issue: main_run.py builds its save path as `f'./{args.results_path}/'` (main_run.py line ~137) -- plain string concatenation, not os.path.join. Passing an absolute --results_path does NOT make the output land there; it gets glued onto './' and resolves relative to the script's CWD.
repo_quirk_found.actual_output_location: ended up at code/workspace/AudioEditingCode/results_zeta_vibrato/... (nested under the code/ dir we ran from) instead of the intended /workspace/AudioEditingCode/results_zeta_vibrato/
repo_quirk_found.workaround_used: just located and copied the files from the actual nested path rather than patching the script
repo_quirk_found.affects: main_run.py and main_run_sdedit.py only (main_pc_extract_inv.py / main_pc_apply_drift.py use os.path.join correctly and were not affected)

outputs.orig.wav: true source clip, re-synthesized (mel + HiFi-GAN vocoding)
outputs.zeta_vibrato_edit.wav: the text-based edited output (target prompt applied, tstart=100)

comparison_purpose: Listen against run1/run2/run3's PCA-based vibrato attempts. If this sounds like a cleaner, more controlled vibrato increase without the PCA runs' instrumental-balance shifts or in-edit weirdness, that's evidence the instability we've been chasing is specific to ZEUS's unsupervised-direction-discovery step, not to this DDPM-inversion backbone in general.
